children: The Nifty50 may still be about 9% below its all-time high, but a growing number of stocks across the broader market are climbing to their yearly peaks, signalling a strengthening rally beyond the benchmark index.

From Bajaj Auto to Ather Energy and Welspun Corp, as many as 94 companies with a market capitalisation of at least ₹500 crore hit their 52-week highs on Tuesday, September 1, even as market breadth remained weak, with more stocks declining than advancing. Nearly two stocks declined for every one that gained on Tuesday.

According to a CNBC-TV analysis, the number of stocks scaling their 52-week highs rose sharply to 94 on Tuesday, from 61 on Monday and around 35 on Friday. This means that nearly 5% of the roughly 2,000 companies with a market capitalisation of at least ₹500 crore hit their 52-week highs on Tuesday.

Bajaj Auto was the only Nifty50 constituent to hit a 52-week high on Tuesday. JSW Steel and Titan had previously tested their yearly highs on August 27. Around 25 companies each from the sample had hit their 52-week highs on August 26 and August 27, according to data compiled from Bloomberg.
The breadth of the rally comes even as market participants expect earnings growth among large-cap companies to remain slower than that of mid- and small-cap stocks.

“Large-cap earnings growth is currently lower than that of the Nifty Junior and mid-cap indices. We do not expect Nifty earnings CAGR to exceed 10–12% from here,” said Rana Gupta, Senior Portfolio Manager and India Equity Specialist at Manulife Investment Management.

The combined market capitalisation of the companies that hit their 52-week highs on Tuesday stood at ₹10.9 lakh crore, with Bajaj Auto accounting for nearly a third of the aggregate market capitalisation.
Among the stocks, Welspun Corp has delivered the strongest gains, rallying 214% since the start of the year. Ather Energy has gained nearly 130% over the same period.
Several other stocks have more than doubled in 2026. Sansera Engineering is up 133% year to date, while Happy Forgings has gained 111%, Shilpa Medicare 177% and Avalon Technologies 164%.

The strength in the broader market is also evident in the performance of the mid- and small-cap indices. Both are trading near record highs and have gained 5% and 12%, respectively, since the start of the year, compared with an 8% decline in the Nifty50 over the same period.

title: Nearly 100 stocks hit 52-week highs even as Nifty remains well below its peak
